issues.description: ALTER TABLE rewrite drops the outer Delimited, silently narrowing the grammar to a single action per statement.
issues.detail: The previous form accepted comma-delimited top-level actions (e.g. ADD column_b ..., DROP COLUMN ...) — the exact example deleted from the fixtures. The new bare OneOf permits only one action. If T-SQL genuinely forbids this, document it in a code comment and cite the spec; otherwise this is a regression masked by fixture deletion.

issues.description: DROP COLUMN and DROP CONSTRAINT collapsed under a shared DROP head, eroding structural dispatch and admitting inconsistent forms.
issues.detail: Folding both DROP variants under one outer keyword with inner Delimited(Sequence(...)) forces downstream rules to disambiguate by lookahead rather than named subtype. The optional per-element CONSTRAINT keyword also permits mixed lists like 'DROP CONSTRAINT a, b, CONSTRAINT c'. Split into named AlterTableDropColumn/AlterTableDropConstraint subgrammars or tighten the inner shape.

issues.description: DEFAULT_LANGUAGE now accepts NumericLiteralSegment with no fixture and no documented rationale.
issues.detail: The OneOf adds a numeric branch (presumably for LCID integers) but no test exercises DEFAULT_LANGUAGE=1033 and the PR description omits it. Either add a one-line fixture and a comment noting the LCID form, or drop the branch. Untested parser branches accumulate as silent surface area.

issues.description: IdentityGrammar repeats the (optional sign, numeric) pair and admits values the engine rejects without a documented contract.
issues.detail: The seed/increment shape is duplicated; a named SignedNumericLiteralSegment used twice would remove the repetition and prevent drift. The grammar also admits forms like '+2' or '--2' that T-SQL semantics reject. State the parser-is-permissive contract in a comment and consolidate the rule.

issues.description: AlterTableStatementSegment is a sprawling OneOf better expressed as named per-keyword subgrammars.
issues.detail: The branch list is effectively a dispatch table keyed by ADD/DROP/ALTER/SET/REBUILD/RENAME. Lifting each branch to a named grammar (AlterTableAddSegment, AlterTableDropSegment, etc.) makes the structure self-evident, restores named subtypes for downstream consumers, and allows independent fixture coverage per branch.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the PR is a useful TSQL parser extension with reasonable fixtures, but the AlterTableStatementSegment rewrite is the central concern: removing the outer Delimited silently narrows accepted syntax and the deleted multi-action fixture conceals whether this is intentional. Folding DROP COLUMN and DROP CONSTRAINT under a shared head erodes structural dispatch and admits inconsistent surface forms. The DEFAULT_LANGUAGE numeric branch and the IDENTITY signed-literal handling both ship without documented contracts or fixtures exercising the new admissions. Ship after stating the intended grammar surface, restoring or justifying the removed multi-action form, and adding the missing fixtures.
